names.name: extra crispy
names.said: 'Extra crispy' at the register; 'well done' on the ticket.

etymology.root: extra (Latin extra 'outside, beyond') + crispy (Old English crisp, from Latin crispus 'curled', re-pointed in English to mean brittle) — an intensifier stuck to a texture word
etymology.note: *Inference —* the phrase is an instruction wearing the grammar of a flavour. It goes in the same slot on the ticket as 'hot' or 'lemon pepper', but it asks the fryer for time rather than the sauce station for anything.

text.what: An order for more time in the oil. Not a flavour, not an upcharge in most places: a request that the wing stay down until the skin goes hard and the colour goes past golden. Kitchens read it as a range, which is why the same words get you different wings at two counters a block apart.
text.how: A cook answers it three ways — leave them longer in one fry, pull the basket up and drop it back for a second hit, or run the whole order through a proper double fry. Ordering it costs minutes, so a busy kitchen will sometimes decline. Ask for it and for sauce on the side and the crust survives the drive home; ask for it and a heavy toss and you have undone it.
